items.headline: Splatoon Raiders hits 9.4/10 — highest-rated Nintendo franchise game ever
items.why: Single-player, not extraction. You were relieved when it wasn't a Marathon-style extraction shooter — a month later it's the best-reviewed game Nintendo's ever put its franchise name on.

items.headline: FFVII Revelation: Queen's Blood is back — and Red XIII, not Cloud, runs the story this time
items.why: The minigame you never skip gets its own arc. Nanaki's boat-deck card obsession from Rebirth becomes an entire storyline in Revelation, with the rules rebalanced from scratch.

items.headline: Switch 2 quietly gets a hardware revision — user-replaceable battery, no thermal paste to fight
items.why: Pure hardware-nerd bait: EU units now ship with visible Joy-Con rail screws and a battery you can pop out without redoing thermal paste. Capacity drops under 1%, console gets ~10g heavier. Rolling out beyond Europe eventually.

items.headline: Asha Sharma flew to Tokyo to personally sign Kojima Productions' wall after the PHYSINT deal
items.why: This is the specific Xbox story worth your attention, not the marketing wire — Sharma in a Kojima Productions hoodie, days after Sony walked away from PHYSINT and Xbox picked it up. Real director-level engagement, not a press release.

items.headline: GTA 6's cops now remember your face, your car, and your gun — even after you lose them
items.why: Not hype-of-the-day, just the design detail that matters: a new 'heat' system tracks what police actually know about you (clothes, vehicle, weapon) even after your stars drop. GTA 5's shrug-off-anything policing is gone. Nov 19 still holds, preload opens Nov 12.

items.headline: Crash Bandicoot turned 30 this month — and got a Fortnite skin and not much else
items.why: "I love crash bandicoot tbh" — well, Activision marked the actual 30th anniversary (Sept 9) with anniversary art and a 1,500 V-Buck skin. A leaker with a real track record (correctly called Spyro: A Realm Beyond) says a new Crash is greenlit, but cautions it's years out. Corporate-cheerful, not the real thing yet.

items.headline: SteamOS 3.9.1 preview lands with hibernation groundwork and stability fixes
items.why: Steam Deck defender maintenance patch: fan-speed bug fix, suspend/resume fixes for older RDNA1/2 dGPUs, and early hibernation support. Not flashy, but exactly the kind of upkeep that keeps the "tremendously successful" argument alive.
